overallAssessment.narrative: Reg Sackey-Addo has already done, in production, the core work this role describes: turning ambiguous organizational goals into agent-executable tasks with persistent context, review loops, evaluation, and human-control boundaries. At CModel, he initiated an agentic development model that opened implementation to the whole team while engineers retained architecture, review, and release control, backed by CI/CD, testing, and evals; he also built the strategic assistant and an email-to-decision-intelligence workflow from product definition through production. His track record spans zero-to-one building, integration engineering across OAuth/APIs and third-party systems, and operating workflows through real failure modes — meaning he can discover what agents should do and then actually run it. For a role where demonstrated ability matters more than title, he is the profile: he has shipped human-AI workflows and redesigned how an organization works, not just prototyped them.

themes.title: Discover and scope organizational work suitable for human-AI collaboration, translating ambiguous goals into agent-ready
themes.narrative: Reg has directly performed the discovery-and-scope work this role centers on: at CModel he initiated an agentic development process that identified which work could move to human-plus-agent execution and decomposed it into tasks, context design, and review responsibilities. He selects signals from noisy sources (email-to-decision-intelligence) rather than dumping raw data into models, and pairs schema-constrained generation with validation and accept/retry/reject boundaries so probabilistic output becomes trustworthy application state. That combination of opportunity-spotting, specification discipline, and human-control design is exactly the role's core.

themes.title: Design persistent context, task specifications, review loops, and human-control boundaries for agent workflows
themes.narrative: Reg's CModel work is a direct match: he created shared technical documentation as persistent context for coding agents and humans, established engineer review loops for human- and agent-generated changes, and kept architecture, validation, and release as human-controlled boundaries. In products, he assembles task-specific runtime context from application state and tool calls rather than overloading prompts, and separates model choice from workflow design so behavior stays stable as models change.

themes.title: Define evaluation criteria and verification methods to know when agent workflows actually work
themes.narrative: Reg treats verification as a design problem, not an afterthought: he built evals for AI behavior where deterministic tests are insufficient, made acceptance criteria executable where possible, and uses schema-constrained generation with explicit validation and repair/reject paths to create a firm boundary between model output and application state. His stated working method — inspect failures and adjust the task, context, or model rather than treating repeated generation as progress — is the evaluation mindset this role needs.

themes.title: Prototype and integrate workflows connecting agents, internal tools, and external systems
themes.narrative: Reg has built and integrated agent-connected workflows across internal and external systems: the CModel strategic assistant (Next.js/Vercel AI SDK) with tool calling against application data and web search, OAuth/API integrations across Microsoft 365, SharePoint, Teams, DocuSign, HubSpot, and others, and an email-to-decision-intelligence pipeline he owned end to end. At MusicBreakr he engineered recurring ingestion across four social platforms under real quota and scheduling constraints, showing he can prototype and harden cross-system workflows in production.

themes.title: Operationalize successful workflows and carry them through real use and failure modes
themes.narrative: Reg's workflows run in production, not demos: the email pipeline and strategic assistant operate in CModel's product, and he has maintained OAuth token lifecycle and debugged failures at system boundaries — expired authorization, unexpected external state, APIs diverging from documentation. At MusicBreakr he operated recurring ingestion under quota limits and debugged production failures across payment systems and third-party APIs, and he built Reaccord end to end as an independent product, demonstrating he carries workflows through real use.

interviewQuestions: Walk through how you decided which work at CModel could move to human-plus-agent execution — how did you identify candidates, and what made you reject some?
When an agent workflow's output fails validation or looks wrong in production, what is your actual debugging and adjustment process, and how do you decide when to tighten human control?
How did you measure whether the agentic development process at CModel actually improved throughput or quality, and what would you build first here to evaluate agent workflows?
